source.title: Manassantin A inhibits tumour growth under hypoxia through the activation of chaperone-mediated autophagy by modulating Hsp90 activity.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Hypoxia tumor models using ManA, MK-2206, 17-AAG, TFEB siRNA, Flag-Hsp90alpha overexpression, HIF-1alpha/Hsc70 IP, luciferase refolding, and CMA readouts.
evidence_limitations: The study explicitly notes ManA does not directly interact with tested Hsp90 domains and the source does not test TFEB-HSP90 binding. HSP90alpha is resolved by overexpression and database context, but inhibitor effects remain broad cytosolic Hsp90 pharmacology.
claim_summary: Manassantin A indirectly modulates cytosolic Hsp90/Hsp90alpha function by disrupting Hsp90-ATP synthase interaction, activates CMA, increases TFEB nuclear localization, and promotes HIF-1alpha degradation. Flag-Hsp90alpha overexpression rescues HIF-1alpha after ManA, but TFEB is downstream pathway context rather than an HSP90 interactor or client.

source.title: Persistent Activation of mRNA Translation by Transient Hsp90 Inhibition.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are mentioned without a necessarily resolved comparison; no specificity is inferred.
model_context: Translation-regulator LUMIER screen, endogenous HSP90 IP, CPEB2 full-length versus delta-PrD AP-MS, and radicicol/STA9090 inhibitor-induced oligomerization assays.
evidence_limitations: Alpha and beta are both mentioned but not isoform-separated functionally. The evidence is strong direct or near-direct association and inhibitor-sensitive conformational regulation, but purified binding and classical client-rescue evidence are incomplete.
claim_summary: CPEB2 is a strong cytosolic HSP90 interactor and candidate-client/conformational-regulator source. A LUMIER screen and endogenous IP validate CPEB2-HSP90 association, AP-MS identifies HSP90AA/HSP90AB as PrD-dependent CPEB2 interactors, and HSP90 inhibitors promote CPEB2 oligomerization.

source.title: HSP90alpha is needed for the survival of rod photoreceptors and regulates the expression of rod PDE6 subunits.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Hsp90aa1 global knockout mouse retina at P15/P30/P45/P80; Aipl1 heterozygous mouse retina; bovine retina IP-MS statement; TMT proteomics, immunoblot, qRT-PCR, IP, IHC/IF, and ERG.
evidence_limitations: Direct AIPL1-HSP90alpha interaction evidence is stated as data-not-shown IP-MS and prior-literature context, not an inspected primary figure in this source. HSP90beta is discussed as compensatory/contextual but not tested as an AIPL1 regulator in the same way. Local supplements appear to be HTML stubs despite Office/PDF-like filenames.
claim_summary: HSP90alpha loss in mouse retina reduces AIPL1 and rod PDE6 protein abundance post-transcriptionally. AIPL1 is framed as an HSP90 cochaperone/PDE6 assembly factor, but this source supports HSP90AA1-dependent AIPL1 abundance regulation more strongly than direct HSP90-AIPL1 binding.

source.title: Lysine butyrylation of HSP90 regulated by KAT8 and HDAC11 confers chemoresistance.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: KYSE150/KYSE410 ESCC cells and 5-FU-resistant derivatives; HSP90-WT/K754R, HDAC11 and KAT8 knockdown/overexpression/catalytic mutants; purified GST-HSP90 pull-downs with HDAC11-His and KAT8-His; in vitro deacylase and butyrylation assays; CHX stability and ubiquitination assays; 5-FU chemoresistance models.
evidence_limitations: The relationship is regulation of HSP90AA1 modification and stability, not HDAC11 or KAT8 as HSP90 clients. HSP90AB1/beta is not compared. Supplementary files in the local archive are retrieval stubs or recaptcha pages, so supplement tables were not independently reviewed.
claim_summary: This source strongly supports HDAC11 and KAT8 as direct/proximal upstream regulators of HSP90AA1 K754 butyrylation and HSP90 stability. The manuscript states that HSP90AA1 is referred to as HSP90 throughout. HSP90 K754 butyrylation is identified by MS and validated by IP/western; K754R impairs HSP90 stability and chemoresistance. HDAC11 binds HSP90 by endogenous co-IP and purified HSP90-GST pull-down, HDAC11 knockdown increases HSP90 Kbu, inactive HDAC11 loses activity, and in vitro deacylase assays support HDAC11 as the eraser. KAT8 similarly binds HSP90, increases HSP90 Kbu, loses activity as a catalytic mutant, and directly butyrylates HSP90 in vitro.

source.title: Lysine butyrylation of HSP90 regulated by KAT8 and HDAC11 confers chemoresistance.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: KYSE150/KYSE410 ESCC cells and 5-FU-resistant derivatives; HSP90 IP-MS and proteomics overlap; SDCBP overexpression/knockdown/truncation and HSP90 mutant constructs; docking and co-IP; V020-9974 SPR and compound disruption assays; AKT/TS readouts; xenograft and PDX 5-FU response.
evidence_limitations: SDCBP is an upstream HSP90 regulator/stabilizer, not an HSP90 client. Direct binding is supported by co-IP, domain mapping, docking, and compound competition, but a purified SDCBP-HSP90 binding assay is not shown in the reviewed main figures. V020-9974 interpretation carries compound/off-target caveats. HSP90AB1/beta is not compared. Local supplement files are retrieval stubs or recaptcha pages.
claim_summary: This source strongly supports SDCBP as an HSP90AA1-associated upstream stabilizer/regulator. HSP90 IP-MS intersected with resistant-cell proteomics nominates SDCBP; endogenous and exogenous co-IP validate SDCBP-HSP90 association; SDCBP overexpression increases HSP90 Kbu and HSP90 protein while SDCBP knockdown decreases them; CHX assays show SDCBP stabilizes HSP90; SDCBP PDZ2 and HSP90 amino acids 208-218 mediate the interaction; SDCBP competes with HDAC11 for HSP90 binding; and V020-9974 binds SDCBP PDZ2, disrupts SDCBP-HSP90, increases HDAC11-HSP90, lowers HSP90 Kbu/expression, and sensitizes ESCC PDX models to 5-FU.

source.title: Inhibition of HSP90 in Driver Oncogene-Defined Lung Adenocarcinoma Cell Lines: Key Proteins Underpinning Therapeutic Efficacy.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are compared; the scope alone does not establish an isoform-exclusive relationship.
model_context: Eleven lung adenocarcinoma cell lines grouped by EGFR mutation, KRAS mutation, EML4-ALK translocation, or triple-negative status; 17-AAG, IPI-504, STA-9090, AUY-922, VER-155008, and combined HSP90alpha/HSP90beta siRNA; HSP90alpha/HSP70/client western blot validation; iTRAQ/NanoLC-MS/MS proteomics and pathway enrichment.
evidence_limitations: ASS1 is absent from the queued Fig2-Fig4 display text and appears in the manuscript as a downstream iTRAQ/pathway interpretation. The local supplementary ZIP is a tiny retrieval stub and was not independently reviewable, so the ASS1 quantitative proteomics values were not checked in a local supplement table. HSP90alpha and HSP90beta are jointly silenced for proteomics and are not used to assign an ASS1 isoform-specific dependency.
claim_summary: This source supports ASS1 only as a subtype-specific proteomic/pathway response marker after HSP90 inhibition in lung adenocarcinoma models. HSP90 inhibitors and combined HSP90alpha/HSP90beta siRNA are validated, iTRAQ proteomics identifies subtype-dependent response programs, and the text reports increased ASS1 after HSP90 inhibition in EML4-ALK-translocated lines and reduced ASS1 in EGFR-mutated lines within an arginine-biosynthesis pathway context. The manuscript does not test ASS1 binding to HSP90, HSP90-dependent ASS1 stability, or ASS1 client biology.

source.title: Proteomic analysis identifies HSP90AA1, PTK2B, and ANXA2 in the human entorhinal cortex in Alzheimer's disease: Potential role in synaptic homeostasis and Abeta pathology through microglial and astroglial cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Postmortem human entorhinal cortex from AD and non-AD cases; DIA proteomics and IPA/SYNGO/BioGRID analysis; western blot validation in five cases per group; IF/confocal localization in seven cases per group; neuronal, microglial, astroglial, Abeta, and tau pathology markers.
evidence_limitations: The source is human disease proteomic/pathway context only. Western blot validation trends for HSP90AA1, PTK2B, and ANXA2 were not statistically significant. ANXA2 IF increased significantly in AD, but that is not HSP90-dependent. The IPA/BioGRID interactome is predicted/curated network context and does not establish direct HSP90AA1-ANXA2 or HSP90AA1-PTK2B binding. Local supplement files for Figure S1 and Dataset S1 are invalid retrieval stubs.
claim_summary: This source identifies HSP90AA1, PTK2B, and ANXA2 as AD entorhinal-cortex proteins of interest from proteomics/pathway analysis. HSP90AA1 and PTK2B are reported as downregulated DEPs and ANXA2 as an upregulated DEP, then validated by western blot trends and IF/confocal localization with neurons/glia and Abeta/tau pathology. The manuscript does not test HSP90AA1 binding to ANXA2 or PTK2B, nor HSP90-dependent client/stability regulation of either protein.

source.title: A Cullin 5-based complex serves as an essential modulator of ORF9b stability in SARS-CoV-2 replication.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: HEK293T overexpression/co-IP/ubiquitination/CHX assays; Calu3 and HCT116 ORF9b perturbation assays; SARS-CoV-2 infected Calu3 cells; GA/17-AAG, MG132, CUL5/TOM70/HSP90alpha/HSP90beta perturbations; public scRNA context.
evidence_limitations: This is not evidence that CUL5 is an HSP90 client. Several queue rows mainly measure HSP90alpha-ORF9b or inhibitor/viral phenotypes where CUL5 is not the primary readout. The structural complex is AlphaFold-predicted, and HSP90 inhibitors are not HSP90AA1-specific. Local supplements appear to be HTML stubs.
claim_summary: CUL5 participates in a TOM70-CUL5-HSP90alpha complex regulating SARS-CoV-2 ORF9b stability. CUL5 promotes ORF9b ubiquitination/degradation, while HSP90alpha stabilizes ORF9b; TOM70 bridges ORF9b into the complex.

source.title: Intrinsic signaling pathways modulate targeted protein degradation.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: PROTAC systems with MZ1 and other degraders, luminespib, 17-AAG, HSP90 knockdown, protein degradation, ubiquitylation, and cell-death assays.
evidence_limitations: The manuscript frames HSP90 as a proteostatic pathway modifier of targeted degradation rather than a direct target-client pair. HSP90 effects may occur downstream of ternary complex formation and ubiquitination.
claim_summary: HSP90 inhibitors and HSP90 knockdown enhance PROTAC-induced degradation of BRD4 and related targets, including BRD4/CDK9 degrader contexts, but HSP90 inhibition alone does not destabilize BRD4 and the source does not show direct HSP90-BRD4, HSP90-CDK9, or HSP90-CRBN binding.

source.title: Proteomic analysis of serum small extracellular vesicles identifies diagnostic biomarkers for neuroblastoma.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Serum sEV proteomics in healthy controls, neuroblastoma, and non-NB tumors; NB SEQC transcriptomic prognosis dataset; MRM validation; western blot validation of BSG, HSP90AB1, SLC44A1, CHGA, and ITGAL in 12 healthy control and 12 neuroblastoma samples.
evidence_limitations: The source is diagnostic/prognostic biomarker discovery, not HSP90 biology. Co-occurrence in a biomarker panel does not imply an HSP90 interaction. HSP90AB1 and ITGAL are not detected in the western blot validation. Local supplemental image/table files are retrieval stubs.
claim_summary: This source is a serum small extracellular vesicle diagnostic biomarker/proteomics study in neuroblastoma. BSG, HSP90AB1, SLC44A1, CHGA, ITGAL, and other proteins are assessed as candidate biomarkers by label-free proteomics, MRM, transcriptomic prognosis association, ROC modeling, and western blot validation. The queued BSG/ITGAL rows do not test physical association, client status, regulation, or pathway dependence with HSP90AB1. Supplementary Figure 2 explicitly reports that HSP90AB1 and ITGAL were not detected by western blot, while BSG and CHGA were detected.

source.title: HSP90AA1 restrains clear cell renal cell carcinoma progression by promoting CADM1 expression and suppressing the PI3K-AKT pathway through interaction with FBXO7.

claim_summary: This source supports an HSP90AA1-resolved FBXO7 relationship in ccRCC. Fig7 places FBXO7 downstream of HSP90AA1 for CADM1/PI3K-AKT pathway readouts.

source.title: The molecular chaperone Hsp90alpha is required for meiotic progression of spermatocytes beyond pachytene in the mouse.

model_context: Mouse Hsp90aa1 gene-trap mutant testes during the first spermatogenic wave; P12-P44 immunoblot panel for Hsp90alpha, cyclin B, Cdc2, phospho-Cdc2, NASP, Hsp70-2, and GAPDH; supplemental second gene-trap line supports phenotype/model context.
evidence_limitations: NASP reduction is measured in whole-testis extracts where germ-cell composition changes over time; the authors explicitly caution about altered cell populations. source.title: Hsp90 regulates NADPH oxidase activity and is necessary for superoxide but not hydrogen peroxide production.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are compared; the scope alone does not establish an isoform-exclusive relationship.
model_context: COS-7 cells expressing NOX constructs; HEK293 cells stably expressing NOX5; human neutrophils for NOX2 superoxide; Hsp90alpha, Hsp90beta, and GRP94 siRNA; GA, 17-AAG, and radicicol inhibitor treatments; NOX1/NOX3/NOX4 chimeras; isolated NOX5 enzyme activity assay; BRET proximity assays.
evidence_limitations: NOX5 has the strongest direct client evidence. NOX1 and NOX3 are supported mainly by pharmacologic sensitivity and C-terminal chimera logic, not by direct NOX1/NOX3-Hsp90 binding assays in the reviewed figures. Hsp90 inhibitor effects include compound-context caveats, and the main direct binding assay uses an overexpressed NOX5 C-terminal fragment rather than full-length endogenous NOX5.
claim_summary: This source supports NOX5 as a strong shared cytosolic Hsp90 client/activity-stability target. Hsp90alpha and Hsp90beta knockdown reduce NOX5-derived superoxide while GRP94 knockdown does not; supplemental Hsp90 increases isolated NOX5 enzyme activity; the NOX5 C-terminal domain reciprocally co-immunoprecipitates with Hsp90alpha and Hsp90beta; BRET supports proximity in intact cells; and longer Hsp90 inhibition lowers NOX5 abundance. NOX1 and NOX3 are supported as related Hsp90-sensitive NADPH oxidase targets by inhibitor and chimera data, but direct binding is best established for NOX5 in this source.

source.title: Pnck induces ligand-independent EGFR degradation by probable perturbation of the Hsp90 chaperone complex.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are mentioned without a necessarily resolved comparison; no specificity is inferred.
model_context: HEK293 Neo/HA-PNCK models, geldanamycin, MG132, Hsp90 co-IP, Hsp90 phosphosite MS, EGFR degradation, cell-density assays, and PNCK kinase-mutant comparisons.
evidence_limitations: PNCK-HSP90 evidence is co-IP and pharmacologic/proteostatic, not purified binding. Much of the phenotype is PNCK-induced EGFR degradation and Hsp90 phosphorylation/complex perturbation. Alpha and beta are both seen in phosphoproteomics but not separately functionally assigned.
claim_summary: PNCK is supported as a shared cytosolic HSP90 client-like kinase and HSP90-complex perturbation source. PNCK coimmunoprecipitates with Hsp90, geldanamycin destroys PNCK and enhances EGFR degradation, PNCK-induced EGFR degradation coincides with proteasomal PNCK loss, and Hsp90 alpha/beta phosphorylation changes are detected by mass spectrometry.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are mentioned without a necessarily resolved comparison; no specificity is inferred.

evidence_limitations: The Hsp90A/B MS band and pan-Hsp90 assays support cytosolic Hsp90-family client evidence but do not resolve alpha versus beta specificity.

The source identifies Hsp90A/B and Cdc37 with FGFR3 by IP/MS and co-IP, shows endogenous reciprocal Hsp90-FGFR3 association, shows Hsp90 inhibitors disrupt FGFR3-Hsp90 binding, and shows 17-AAG-dependent FGFR3 destabilization, ubiquitination, degradation, and reduced signaling.

source.title: SAHA shows preferential cytotoxicity in mutant p53 cancer cells by destabilizing mutant p53 through inhibition of the HDAC6-Hsp90 chaperone axis.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Mutant-p53 cancer models; SAHA/HDAC6 inhibition; Hsp90-mutp53 association; MDM2/CHIP degradation machinery; proteasomal stability and apoptosis assays.
evidence_limitations: HSP90 relationship belongs mainly to mutant p53 as a client and HDAC6 as a chaperone regulator; MDM2 is downstream E3 context.
claim_summary: HDAC6 and MDM2 are support-only regulatory context in the Hsp90-mutant p53 chaperone axis. HDAC6 regulates Hsp90 chaperone function, while MDM2 participates in downstream mutant-p53 degradation after SAHA, but neither is supported as an HSP90 client.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Huntington disease cell models and mHtt clearance screen; AUY922/Hsp90 inhibition; co-IP; soluble full-length mHtt abundance; proteasome-linked clearance assays.
evidence_limitations: Alpha/beta specificity is unresolved, and inhibitor data carry compound-level caveats despite physical association support.

source.title: A unifying model for mTORC1-mediated regulation of mRNA translation.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: mTOR inhibition and 4E-BP/eIF4E translational regulation experiments using TOP/TOP-like mRNA translation and eIF4E binding readouts.
evidence_limitations: The evidence is RNA/translational regulation of the Hsp90ab1 transcript. It should not be interpreted as an MTOR-HSP90 protein complex, HSP90 client, or isoform-specific chaperone relationship.
claim_summary: Hsp90ab1 is presented as a TOP-like mRNA whose translation is regulated by mTORC1/4E-BP/eIF4E mechanisms. This is HSP90AB1 transcript-level regulation, not HSP90 protein-interaction or client evidence.

source.title: Smyd1b is required for skeletal and cardiac muscle function in zebrafish.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Zebrafish embryo smyd1b knockdown myofibrillogenesis model; HEK293 overexpression co-IP for Myc-Smyd1b isoforms with Flag-Unc45b or Flag-Hsp90alpha1; qRT-PCR/in situ expression of hsp90alpha1 and unc45b; myosin protein and mRNA readouts.
evidence_limitations: Primary Fig7 co-IP is Smyd1b-Unc45b and Smyd1b-Hsp90alpha1, not Unc45b-Hsp90alpha1. The assay uses HEK293 overexpression of tagged zebrafish constructs. The source itself says purified-protein pull-downs are needed for direct Smyd1b binding. It should not supersede PMC2377097 as the primary UNC45B-HSP90 cochaperone/direct-complex source.
claim_summary: This source supports a Smyd1b-centered myofibrillogenesis model in which Hsp90alpha1 and Unc45b are myosin-chaperone machinery context. Smyd1b knockdown up-regulates hsp90alpha1 and unc45b expression and reduces myosin protein accumulation. Figure 7 shows Smyd1b-tv1 co-immunoprecipitates separately with Flag-Unc45b and Flag-Hsp90alpha1. The paper does not directly assay an Unc45b-Hsp90alpha1 interaction in Figure 7, and the discussion states that purified-protein pull-downs would be needed to show direct Smyd1b binding to UNC-45b or Hsp90alpha1.

source.title: HSP90alpha plays an important role in piRNA biogenesis and retrotransposon repression in mouse.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.

evidence_limitations: FKBP6 is not experimentally manipulated or measured in the queued figures from this source. claim_summary: This source supports HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha function in mouse piRNA biogenesis, MIWI2 localization, and retrotransposon repression, but the queued FKBP6 rows are pathway/context only. It concludes that HSP90alpha has both FKBP6-dependent and FKBP6-independent roles. The reviewed queued figures do not measure FKBP6 protein, FKBP6-HSP90 binding, or FKBP6-dependent HSP90 client biology.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are compared; the scope alone does not establish an isoform-exclusive relationship.

evidence_limitations: The source explicitly argues CacyBP/SIP is not an Hsp90 client. claim_summary: CacyBP/SIP is a cytosolic Hsp90-binding chaperone/cochaperone-machinery regulator: it co-IPs with Hsp90alpha and Hsp90beta, maps to Hsp90beta middle-domain-containing constructs, shows PLA and purified-protein ELISA binding, retains binding after Hsp90 inhibitor treatment, has chaperone-like activity, and shifts Hsp90 pI patterns consistent with possible dephosphorylation.

source.title: Mitochondrial PKM2 regulates oxidative stress-induced apoptosis by stabilizing Bcl2.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: U87/U251 glioblastoma systems; H2O2 oxidative stress; HSP90AA1 shRNA and rHSP90alpha1 WT/G97D rescue; recombinant HSP90alpha1/GST-PKM2/His-Bcl2 chaperone and kinase assays; 17-AAG supplementary context; Bcl2 T69 and Cul3-Rbx1 degradation pathway assays.
evidence_limitations: The active queue rows were keyed to BCL2 and CUL3, but the direct HSP90AA1-regulated substrate is PKM2. Local supplementary files are HTML/download stubs, so Supplementary FigS3/FigS4 and tables were source-text-supported rather than independently visualized. The biology is oxidative-stress/glioma-model specific.
claim_summary: The source supports PKM2 as an HSP90AA1/HSP90alpha1 client-like conformational substrate under oxidative stress. HSP90alpha1 interacts with PKM2, recombinant HSP90alpha1 WT but not ATPase-dead G97D exposes a PKM2 epitope and enables PKM2-Bcl2 binding, and HSP90alpha1 WT rescue supports Bcl2 stability. BCL2 is downstream, stabilized by PKM2-dependent T69 phosphorylation that blocks Cul3-Rbx1 recruitment; CUL3 is the downstream E3 ligase axis rather than an HSP90 interactor.

source.title: Promotion of Myoblast Differentiation by Fkbp5 via Cdk4 Isomerization.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are mentioned without a necessarily resolved comparison; no specificity is inferred.
model_context: C2C12 mouse myoblast differentiation and knockdown models; FLAG-tagged FKBP4/FKBP5 AP-MS; endogenous Hsp90alpha/beta IP; FKBP4/FKBP5 knockdown; CDK4 phosphorylation, Rb phosphorylation, PPIase peptide assay, and myoblast differentiation phenotypes.
evidence_limitations: The Hsp90 IP is alpha/beta pooled and does not compare HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1. The main direct Hsp90 evidence is co-IP/AP-MS complex membership, while FKBP5-specific enzymatic isomerization is shown for CDK4 rather than Hsp90. The context is mouse C2C12 myogenesis and should not be generalized to all FKBP4/FKBP5 client contexts without additional sources.
claim_summary: FKBP4 and FKBP5 are supported as cytosolic Hsp90-associated cochaperone/complex regulators for CDK4 in C2C12 myoblasts. FLAG-FKBP4/FKBP5 AP-MS nominates Hsp90alpha, Hsp90beta, CDK4, and CDC37; Figure 4B shows endogenous Hsp90alpha/beta IP co-precipitates CDK4, Fkbp4, and Fkbp5; Figure 4C shows FKBP4 or FKBP5 knockdown reduces CDK4 recovery in Hsp90alpha/beta IP without lowering CDK4 input. The manuscript further distinguishes FKBP5-specific CDK4 isomerization/phosphorylation regulation from the shared FKBP4/FKBP5 Hsp90-complex retention function.

source.title: Chaperone-mediated autophagy is involved in the execution of ferroptosis.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are compared; the scope alone does not establish an isoform-exclusive relationship.
model_context: HT-22, 661W/661W-Flag-GPX4, HT1080 HA-HSP90alpha/beta, HEK293T GPX4/HSC70 cotransfection; erastin, glutamate, RSL3, CDDO; lysosome and proteasome inhibitors; HSC70/Lamp2a knockdown/overexpression; GPX4 AP-MS, co-IP, CMA reporter, lysosome fractionation, GPX4 CMA motif mutants.
evidence_limitations: The authors explicitly state HSP90 may not bind GPX4 directly. HSP90 appears to regulate GPX4 degradation via HSC70/Lamp2a/CMA and ferroptosis context. GPX4 should not be scored as a canonical HSP90 client from this source. Supplemental file is an invalid not-PDF/HTML stub.
claim_summary: The source supports GPX4 as an HSP90-linked CMA degradation/stability target during ferroptosis, not as a direct HSP90 client. Ferroptosis induces Lamp2a/CMA; HSP90alpha/beta knockdown and HSP90 inhibitors protect ferroptosis; GPX4 AP-MS identifies increased HSC70 and HSP90 among GPX4-associated proteins after erastin; co-IP supports HSC70-HSP90 and GPX4-HSC70 interactions; HSC70/Lamp2a knockdown restores GPX4; CDDO blocks HSP90-Lamp2a interaction and Lamp2a induction; and GPX4 CMA-motif mutants resist degradation.

source.title: Hsp90B enhances MAST1-mediated cisplatin resistance by protecting MAST1 from proteosomal degradation.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are compared; the scope alone does not establish an isoform-exclusive relationship.
model_context: Cisplatin-resistant KB-3-1, A549, PCI-15A, and A2780 cancer cell systems; 293T GST-MAST1 pulldown/MS; 17-AAG, MG-132, cisplatin, lestaurtinib; hsp90A/hsp90B knockdown comparison; MAST1 WT/2KR rescue; xenografts, PDX, and HNSCC clinical IHC correlation.
evidence_limitations: 17-AAG is a pan-cytosolic Hsp90 inhibitor, and Hsp90A also binds MAST1 detectably, though more weakly and without the same functional knockdown effect. Most direct beta specificity is from isoform comparison/knockdown and Hsp90B SPR/Co-IP, not an isoform-selective inhibitor. Local supplement PDF download is an HTML retrieval stub, so supplemental details were reviewed through article text references rather than a local supplemental PDF.
claim_summary: This source provides high-confidence HSP90AB1/Hsp90B-dominant client evidence for MAST1. GST-MAST1 pulldown/MS nominates Hsp90B, endogenous and exogenous Co-IP validate interaction, Hsp90A is tested and binds more weakly, 17-AAG lowers MAST1 protein without changing MAST1 mRNA, hsp90B knockdown but not hsp90A knockdown explains MAST1 protein/cisplatin-resistance effects, and MAST1 rescue restores hsp90B-knockdown phenotypes. Mechanistically, Hsp90B protects MAST1 from CHIP-mediated ubiquitination at K317/K545 and proteasomal degradation.

source.title: A novel NF-kappaB regulator encoded by circPLCE1 inhibits colorectal carcinoma progression by promoting RPS3 ubiquitin-dependent degradation.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: HCT8 and DLD1 colorectal cancer cells; HEK293T exogenous complex assays with HA-HSP90alpha, His-RPS3, Myc-HSP70, and Flag-circPLCE1-411; circPLCE1 overexpression/knockdown; CHX and MG132; NF-kB p65 nuclear localization/activity; orthotopic and patient-derived xenograft models with RPS3 and p-P65 IHC.
evidence_limitations: The source does not directly perturb HSP90alpha by knockdown or inhibitor in the reviewed figures; instead, circPLCE1-411 disrupts the HSP90alpha/RPS3 complex. Co-IP/IP-MS are association-proximal and not purified direct binding. HSP90beta is not compared. Prior literature is cited for HSP90 protecting RPS3 from proteasomal degradation, so this manuscript should be scored as strong HSP90AA1-resolved candidate-client/stability support rather than a fully standalone validated client source. The local supplement file is an invalid not-PDF/HTML stub.
claim_summary: This source supports RPS3 as an HSP90AA1/HSP90alpha-associated candidate client or stability target in a circPLCE1-411 colorectal-cancer mechanism. circPLCE1-411 IP/MS nominates RPS3 and HSP90alpha; reciprocal IP/western assays show circPLCE1-411, HSP90alpha, and RPS3 association; increasing circPLCE1-411 lowers RPS3 protein without lowering RPS3 RNA, accelerates RPS3 loss, promotes RPS3 ubiquitination, and MG132 rescues RPS3 abundance; increasing circPLCE1-411 reduces RPS3-HSP90alpha association while increasing RPS3-HSP70 association; and HSP90alpha N-terminal constructs support the relevant complex interface. Downstream, RPS3 and p-P65/NF-kB readouts are reduced in cell and xenograft contexts.

source.title: Suppression of breast cancer-associated bone loss with osteoblast proteomes via Hsp90ab1/moesin-mediated inhibition of TGFbeta/FN1/CD44 signaling.

isoform_scope_note: Review found no applicable human Hsp90-family relationship.
model_context: Lrp5-overexpressing MC3T3 osteoblast conditioned medium; EO771 and MDA-MB-231 tumor cells; EO771 extracellular matrix; mouse mammary tumor and osteolysis models; recombinant HSP90AB1/MSN treatment; CD44 and FN1 siRNA.
evidence_limitations: HSP90AB1-LAP/TGF-beta evidence is co-IP from conditioned medium, not purified direct binding. The queued FN1/LRP5/NFATC1 genes are not HSP90 partners in the figure. FN1 is an MSN-associated extracellular matrix protein; LRP5 and NFATC1 are pathway/phenotype nodes. The secretome context is specialized and should not be treated as canonical cytosolic HSP90 client evidence.
claim_summary: This source supports an extracellular HSP90AB1/Hsp90ab1 secretome interaction with latent TGF-beta/LAP in Lrp5-overexpressing osteoblast conditioned medium. Figure 7C shows LAP co-immunoprecipitated by HSP90AB1/Hsp90ab1, while separate MSN IPs recover CD44 and FN1 from EO771 cell lysate or extracellular matrix. The queued FN1/LRP5/NFATC1 candidates are false positives for HSP90 relationship scoring: FN1 belongs to the MSN-CD44/FN1 axis, LRP5 is the upstream Wnt/secretome driver, and NFATC1 is a downstream osteoclast differentiation marker.

source.title: PGK1-coupled HSP90 stabilizes GSK3beta expression to regulate the stemness of breast cancer stem cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: MCF-7ADR breast cancer stem-cell model, 293T Hsp90alpha domain/mutant expression systems, multiple cancer cell lines for PGK1 knockdown/GSK3beta abundance, clinical breast cancer tissue IP, purified His-PGK1/His-GSK3beta/GST-Hsp90alpha domain binding assays, Hsp90 inhibitors HDN-1 and 17-AAG, MG132, mammosphere assays.
evidence_limitations: The strong paper-level client is GSK3beta, not PGK1. PGK1 is a recruiter co-chaperone/adapter. Some Hsp90 co-IP uses pan-Hsp90 antibody and the Hsp90beta contribution is modeled only because a closed Hsp90alpha crystal structure was unavailable. 17-AAG and HDN-1 are pharmacologic perturbations with compound-context caveats. Local supplement PDF is an HTML/not-PDF stub.
claim_summary: This source supports PGK1 as a recruiter co-chaperone/direct HSP90alpha C-domain binding adapter for the GSK3beta client. GSK3beta IP/MS nominated PGK1, reciprocal co-IP and clinical breast-cancer tissue IP show Hsp90-PGK1-GSK3beta complexes, PGK1 knockdown reduces GSK3beta and Hsp90-GSK3beta binding, purified His-PGK1 directly binds GST-C-Hsp90alpha, and PGK1 enables GSK3beta association with C-terminal Hsp90alpha. 17-AAG disrupts PGK1 binding to closed-state Hsp90alpha and the Hsp90alpha-PGK1-GSK3beta complex.

source.title: PGK1-coupled HSP90 stabilizes GSK3beta expression to regulate the stemness of breast cancer stem cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: MCF-7ADR breast cancer stem-cell model, 293T Hsp90alpha domain/mutant expression systems, multiple cancer cell lines for PGK1 knockdown/GSK3beta abundance, clinical breast cancer tissue IP, purified His-PGK1/His-GSK3beta/GST-Hsp90alpha domain binding assays, Hsp90 inhibitors HDN-1 and 17-AAG, MG132, mammosphere assays.
evidence_limitations: The strong paper-level client is GSK3beta, not PGK1. PGK1 is a recruiter co-chaperone/adapter. source.title: A specialized Hsp90 co-chaperone network regulates steroid hormone receptor response to ligand.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: HEK293 tagged FNIP1/FNIP2/Tsc1 IP-MS, co-IP, Hsp90alpha-FLAG catalytic-loop/domain mutants and FNIP/Tsc1 domain mapping; S. cerevisiae pp30 expressing human Hsp90alpha as sole Hsp90 for v-Src, Slt2/RLM1, HSF1, GR, AR, ER, and ligand-binding functional assays.
evidence_limitations: Do not curate FNIP1/FNIP2/TSC1 as Hsp90 clients from this source; they are co-chaperones/chaperone-cycle regulators and downstream clients are steroid hormone receptors, v-Src, Slt2, and HSF1. HSP90AB1/beta is not experimentally tested here; Hsp90beta appears as a structural protomer reference only. Co-IP and domain/truncation assays do not prove purified direct binding and may be affected by tagged overexpression or mutant/truncation conformation. Local supplement PDF/XLSX files are HTML download stubs, so Table S1/S2/S3/S4 were not independently reviewed.
claim_summary: FNIP1, FNIP2, and Tsc1 act as specialized Hsp90 co-chaperones/chaperone-cycle regulators: F1/F2 map Hsp90alpha-associated co-IP/domain interactions and FNIP/Tsc1 complex architecture, while F3/F4 show these co-chaperone combinations tune Hsp90alpha-dependent client activity and steroid hormone receptor ligand responsiveness.

source.title: Chloroquine treatment induces secretion of autophagy-related proteins and inclusion of Atg8-family proteins in distinct extracellular vesicle populations.

isoform_scope_note: Review found no applicable human Hsp90-family relationship.
model_context: MDA-MB-231, SUM159PT, and Hs578T breast cancer cells treated with chloroquine; secreted particle/sEV fractions characterized by western blot, TEM, NTA, TMT proteomics, density gradients, CD63/CD9 immunoaffinity capture, and autophagy cargo markers.
evidence_limitations: HSP90AA1 is used as a known sEV-associated marker and is detected weakly in secreted fractions. The study does not test HSP90AA1 binding, client relationships, isoform-specific function, or regulation of the queued genes. Figure 6 reports that CD63/CD9 IP captured sEV markers but not HSP90AA1.
claim_summary: This source is an autophagy/secreted-particle study after chloroquine treatment, not an HSP90 interaction or client manuscript. HSP90AA1 is detected at low levels in secreted particle fractions in Figure 1 as a known sEV-associated protein. CD63/CD9 immunoprecipitation captures SDCBP/syntenin-1 and TSG101 but not HSP90AA1 in Figure 6. The queued autophagy and sEV marker genes are therefore not HSP90 interactors or clients from this source.

source.title: NudC regulates actin dynamics and ciliogenesis by stabilizing cofilin 1.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: RPE-1, HEK293T and zebrafish NudC/cofilin/ciliogenesis assays; HSP90 evidence mostly from cited/prior co-chaperone context.
evidence_limitations: Direct NudC-cofilin evidence should not be converted into HSP90-NUDC direct evidence. HSP90 inhibitor supplement context does not establish NUDC as an HSP90 target or client.
claim_summary: This source describes NudC as an HSP90 co-chaperone in background and prior interactome context, but the primary inspected experiments in this article center on NudC binding/stabilizing cofilin 1 and regulating actin/ciliogenesis. HSP90 is not the main experimentally resolved partner for NUDC in the reviewed source object.

source.title: NMNAT2:HSP90 Complex Mediates Proteostasis in Proteinopathies.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human AD brain fractions, rTg4510 tauopathy mouse cortex, hTau40 and Ataxin1 aggregation cell models, Cos7/primary neuron assays.
evidence_limitations: The source uses broad HSP90 language and does not resolve HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1. NMNAT2 behaves as a chaperone-like HSP90 partner rather than a client whose stability depends on HSP90.
claim_summary: NMNAT2 complexes with broad cytosolic HSP90 in tau and ataxin aggregation models, and HSP90 perturbation reduces NMNAT2-dependent aggregate clearance/refolding activity. The evidence supports an HSP90-associated chaperone/proteostasis complex, not NMNAT2 as an HSP90 client.

source.title: Heat Shock Protein 90 Modulates Lipid Homeostasis by Regulating the Stability and Function of Sterol Regulatory Element-binding Protein (SREBP) and SREBP Cleavage-activating Protein.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are mentioned without a necessarily resolved comparison; no specificity is inferred.
model_context: HEK293, HepG2, Huh7, CHO/SRD-13A cells, HSP90beta overexpression, HSP90 siRNA, 17-AAG, MG132, CHX and mouse liver inhibitor treatment.
evidence_limitations: The source mentions/detects both cytosolic paralogs but does not experimentally separate alpha versus beta requirement for SCAP. SREBP complex members should be separated in later gene integration.
claim_summary: HSP90 binds the SCAP-SREBP complex, with HSP90alpha and HSP90beta detected in SCAP pulldown/MS, endogenous co-IP of HSP90 with SCAP/SREBP, and HSP90 inhibition/knockdown causing proteasome-dependent SCAP-SREBP degradation with lipid-homeostasis effects.

source.title: HSP90 promotes cell glycolysis, proliferation and inhibits apoptosis by regulating PKM2 abundance via Thr-328 phosphorylation in hepatocellular carcinoma.

isoform_scope_note: Review found no applicable human Hsp90-family relationship.
model_context: HCC clinicopathologic association table where AFP is a patient/tumor marker.
evidence_limitations: Queue extraction attached AFP to a source whose mechanistic HSP90 claim is PKM2/PKM.
claim_summary: AFP appears only as a hepatocellular carcinoma clinical feature associated with HSP90/PKM2-positive tumors, not as an HSP90 binding partner, client, regulated target, or mechanistic protein readout.

source.title: HSP90 promotes cell glycolysis, proliferation and inhibits apoptosis by regulating PKM2 abundance via Thr-328 phosphorylation in hepatocellular carcinoma.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Hep3B, Huh7, HEK293/293T, HCC tissue IHC, HCC xenograft context; HSP90 shRNA, 17-AAG, 17-DMAG, MG132, CHX and PKM2 T328 mutants.
evidence_limitations: The originally listed gene was AFP, but AFP is only a clinical feature in this source. The positive paper-level HSP90 object is PKM2/PKM. HSP90 isoform is unresolved.
claim_summary: The inspected source supports PKM2, encoded by PKM, as the actual HSP90-regulated protein: HSP90 binds PKM2 by AP-MS/co-IP/GST pulldown, HSP90 knockdown or inhibitors reduce PKM2 abundance, proteasome blockade rescues PKM2, and HSP90-GSK3beta-dependent Thr-328 phosphorylation stabilizes PKM2 and supports HCC glycolysis/growth phenotypes.

source.title: HSP90AA1-mediated autophagy promotes drug resistance in osteosarcoma.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: MG-63, Saos-2 and U-2 OS osteosarcoma cells; HSP90AA1 shRNA/overexpression; cisplatin, doxorubicin, methotrexate, docetaxel and xenograft context.
evidence_limitations: The article is HSP90AA1-functional/pathway evidence. HSP90AA1 is source context and MTOR is a downstream pathway readout; neither should be promoted as an ordinary interactor target from this source.
claim_summary: HSP90AA1 is the perturbed HSP90 isoform in this osteosarcoma source, where chemotherapy induces HSP90AA1 and HSP90AA1 knockdown or overexpression modulates autophagy, apoptosis, drug resistance, and PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway readouts. MTOR is downstream pathway context, not an HSP90 client or direct interactor.

source.title: Targeting the Hsp90 C-terminal domain to induce allosteric inhibition and selective client downregulation.

isoform_scope_note: The evidence is Hsp90-family-wide context; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Recombinant HSP90alpha/HSP90beta domain assays and LNCaP prostate cancer cell compound-response blots.
evidence_limitations: BRCA1 downregulation is compound-response evidence without gene-specific HSP90-BRCA1 binding, rescue, or isoform-specific perturbation in the inspected source.
claim_summary: BRCA1 is reported as one of several client proteins downregulated after treatment with HSP90 C-terminal allosteric inhibitors in prostate cancer cells. The source strongly supports compound-HSP90 CTD binding and HSP90 chaperone inhibition, but BRCA1 is a pharmacologic client-downregulation marker rather than a gene-specific direct-binding or stability mechanism in this article.

source.title: NudC L279P Mutation Destabilizes Filamin A by Inhibiting the Hsp90 Chaperoning Pathway and Suppresses Cell Migration.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: RPE-1, HeLa and AGS cells; NudC-L279P overexpression, endogenous/coexpressed IP-MS/co-IP, geldanamycin, radicicol, MG132, CHX and HSP90 rescue.
evidence_limitations: Evidence is unresolved for HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1 and primarily supports NUDC as a cochaperone/regulator in a filamin A stability pathway, not a client.
claim_summary: NudC is reviewed here as an HSP90 cochaperone/chaperone-pathway regulator: NudC interacts with filamin A, HSP90 forms a complex with filamin A, HSP90 ATPase inhibitors reduce filamin A stability, HSP90 overexpression rescues NudC-L279P-associated filamin A stability and migration defects, and supplement evidence places NudC/NudCL/NudCL2 in a filamin A-HSP90 complex.

source.title: Structure of the TELO2-TTI1-TTI2 complex and its function in TOR recruitment to the R2TP chaperone.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Purified human RUVBL1-RUVBL2, TTT and mTOR kinase-region assays, cryo-EM, ATPase assays, pulldowns and XL-MS.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.

source.title: Downregulation of PGAM2 alleviates angiotensin II-induced cardiac hypertrophy by destabilizing HSP90 and inactivating the mTOR/IKKalpha signaling pathway.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, Ang II-induced hypertrophy, rat cardiac hypertrophy models, 293T ubiquitination assays, PGAM2 knockdown/overexpression and HSP90 rescue.
evidence_limitations: The relationship direction is PGAM2 stabilizing/regulating HSP90AA1, not HSP90 stabilizing PGAM2. Cardiomyocyte disease context is narrow.
claim_summary: PGAM2 directly interacts with HSP90AA1, referred to as HSP90 in the work, and stabilizes it in Ang II-induced cardiac hypertrophy models. Co-IP/PLA and residue-mapping support PGAM2-HSP90 interaction, PGAM2 knockdown lowers HSP90 protein without lowering transcript, CHX/ubiquitination assays support HSP90 turnover regulation, and HSP90 restoration rescues downstream mTOR/IKKalpha signaling.

source.title: Downregulation of PGAM2 alleviates angiotensin II-induced cardiac hypertrophy by destabilizing HSP90 and inactivating the mTOR/IKKalpha signaling pathway.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: 293T HSP90 ubiquitination assays and NRVM Ang II/PGAM2-HSP90 stability mechanism.
evidence_limitations: SYVN1 evidence is mechanistically important but narrower than the PGAM2-HSP90 row and is mostly within the HSP90 degradation arm.
claim_summary: SYVN1 is the E3 ubiquitin ligase branch in the source mechanism: PGAM2 competes with SYVN1 for HSP90AA1 interaction and blocks SYVN1-linked HSP90 ubiquitination/degradation. SYVN1 is therefore an HSP90AA1 degradation regulator in this source, not an HSP90 client.

source.title: Structure of the TPR domain of AIP: lack of client protein interaction with the C-terminal alpha-7 helix of the TPR domain of AIP is sufficient for pituitary adenoma predisposition.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are compared; the scope alone does not establish an isoform-exclusive relationship.
model_context: Human AIP TPR-domain crystal structures with HSP90beta/TOMM20 peptides, HSP90alpha peptide comparison, full-length HSP90beta ITC, AIP disease-mutation structural mapping.
evidence_limitations: The strongest structural complex is HSP90beta peptide/full-length beta binding, while alpha is represented by peptide comparison. AIP itself is not a client in this source.
claim_summary: AIP has high-confidence structural and biochemical evidence for binding HSP90 TPR-motif peptides and full-length HSP90beta. Crystal structures resolve AIP TPR bound to HSP90beta EDASRMEEVD peptide, ITC compares HSP90beta, HSP90alpha peptide, HSP70, TOMM20, and PDE4A5 peptide binding, and disease mutations separate chaperone motif binding from client-protein interaction effects.

source.title: Stabilization of integrin-linked kinase by the Hsp90-CHIP axis impacts cellular force generation, migration and the fibrotic response.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Mouse fibroblast ILK-FLAG, CHIP knockout, 17AAG, CHX/MG132/Bafilomycin, recombinant alpha-parvin/ILK/Hsp90 binding, migration and bleomycin-fibrosis models.
evidence_limitations: The article uses broad Hsp90 and 17AAG rather than resolving HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1.
claim_summary: ILK is supported as a broad cytosolic Hsp90 client-like protein: ILK pull-downs recover Hsp90/Hsc70/CHIP, Hsp90 inhibition dissociates ILK from Hsp90 and alpha-parvin, reduces ILK abundance, increases CHIP association/ubiquitination, and proteasome/lysosome blockade attenuates ILK degradation. Hsp90-dependent ILK stabilization is linked to focal-adhesion force generation, migration, and fibrosis phenotypes.

source.title: Hsp90 cochaperones p23 and FKBP4 physically interact with hAgo2 and activate RNA interference-mediated silencing in mammalian cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: HeLa hAgo2 transfection/endogenous co-IP, shRNA knockdown of cochaperones, GFP-let7 reporter RNAi activity, hAgo2 small-RNA loading mutants.
evidence_limitations: Hsp90 isoform is not resolved, and FKBP4 is a cochaperone/adapter, not a client.
claim_summary: FKBP4 is supported as an Hsp90 cochaperone in the hAgo2/RISC maturation pathway: hAgo2 co-IPs with Hsp90, p23, and FKBP4; endogenous hAgo2-p23/FKBP4 interactions are shown; FKBP4 knockdown reduces RNAi efficiency without simply reducing hAgo2/Dicer abundance; and hAgo2 small-RNA-loading mutants prolong Hsp90/cochaperone association.

source.title: HSP90 activity is required for MLKL oligomerisation and membrane translocation and the induction of necroptotic cell death.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Mouse dermal fibroblasts, U937 cells, MLKL mutants, HSP90 inhibitors 17-AAG/NVP-BEP800/AT13387, Cdc37 siRNA, SEC, BN-PAGE, membrane fractionation.
evidence_limitations: HSP90 isoform is unresolved and MLKL stability is not the dominant readout; the evidence is activity/oligomerisation/translocation dependence.
claim_summary: MLKL is the actual HSP90 source object in this article. Multiple HSP90 inhibitors block MLKL-driven necroptosis downstream of RIPK3 activation, HSP90 inhibition prevents MLKL oligomerisation and membrane translocation, Cdc37 knockdown reduces activated MLKL-mediated death, and MLKL transiently co-fractionates/co-IPs with HSP90/Cdc37. MLKL abundance changes are modest and delayed, so the conservative call is candidate-client/activity-localization dependence rather than canonical stability client.

source.title: Evidence for interaction between Hsp90 and the ER membrane complex.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Hsp82/Hsp90, EMC2 deletion and EMC multi-deletion strains, Sti1/Tah1 co-chaperone plasmids, NVP-AUY922 sensitivity, glucocorticoid receptor folding reporter.
evidence_limitations: Primary evidence is yeast Hsp90/Emc2p rather than human EMC2 with HSP90AA1/HSP90AB1. ER membrane-complex context should not be collapsed into human cytosolic isoform specificity.
claim_summary: The article provides yeast evidence for a physical, genetic, and functional relationship between Hsp90 and the ER membrane complex. Flag-Emc2p co-precipitates His-tagged Hsp82/Hsp90, EMC2 deletion modifies Hsp90 inhibitor sensitivity and co-chaperone effects, and multiple EMC deletions impair glucocorticoid receptor folding. This supports a conserved EMC2/Hsp90 interaction hypothesis, but not a human isoform-resolved source-level call.

source.title: A motif in HSP90 and P23 that links molecular chaperones to efficient estrogen receptor alpha methylation by the lysine methyltransferase SMYD2.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are compared; the scope alone does not establish an isoform-exclusive relationship.
model_context: Purified HSP90alpha, HSP90beta, HSP90alpha delta-EEVD, P23, HOP, SMYD2, Alpha assay peptides, and bacterial reconstitution of HSP90/P23-associated ERalpha methylation.
evidence_limitations: The source compares alpha and beta binding but does not claim SMYD2 depends on HSP90 for folding, stability, or maturation.
claim_summary: SMYD2 directly binds both HSP90alpha and HSP90beta in gel-filtration and Alpha assays through a C-terminal HSP90/P23 motif independent of the HSP90 EEVD motif. HSP90/P23 recruitment enhances SMYD2-mediated ERalpha methylation, making SMYD2 an HSP90/P23 direct binding partner that regulates a client-associated modification, not an HSP90 client itself.

source.title: Cryo-EM reveals the remodeling of RUVBL1-RUVBL2 ATPases by the client recruitment component in the HSP90 co-chaperone R2TP.
